ai.description: This slender snake reaches 60–80 cm. It is olive-brown dorsally with a yellow-white belly and a distinct dark stripe through each eye. It features smooth scales and a rounded snout.
ai.identificationRemarks: The Olive Forest Snake is best identified by its distinctively small, blunt head and the presence of a single internasal scale, which separates it from similar colubrids.
ai.habitat: The Olive Forest Snake inhabits moist deciduous and evergreen forests of the Western Ghats, typically found near streams at elevations between 600 and 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: The Olive Forest Snake is primarily nocturnal and semi-aquatic, often foraging for frogs and tadpoles in shallow forest streams and marshy areas.
ai.reproductionNotes: The Olive Forest Snake is oviparous, laying a clutch of 3–7 eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, with eggs deposited in moist soil or leaf litter.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Rhabdops olivaceus* is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, primarily occurring in the states of Karnataka, Kerala, and Tamil Nadu at elevations of 600–1,200 meters.
